item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello! After years of being too lazy to join, I finally made an account. Believe it or not, I've actually been a fan of the SCP Wiki since elementary school, probably around fourth grade? I was introduced to it by my sister, who just really liked giving me nightmares. I was instantly hooked though; I have vivid memories of browsing random articles on the school laptops when I probably wasn't supposed to. I've been in love with horror and weird fiction since, and it's honestly a huge influence on who I am today.

Though I've been a fan for awhile now, I recently rediscovered how much I love this website. For the past few days I've been doing NOTHING but reading SCP articles, drawing fanart, writing fanfic, and resisting the urge to annoy my friends by rambling about it. Now I'm really interested in writing my own SCP, and though I'm super nervous, I'm having a ton of fun coming up with ideas.

I'm constantly amazed by the sheer amount of creativity and talent in this community, and I'm thrilled to eventually contribute to it myself. =)

item.title: Re: The Monster that Didn't Exist
item.content:encoded:
Hey again, thanks for the recrit!

+ Open Response +
- Close -

[…]weird to see a Foundation observation site with no means of self-defense[…].

Again, this would be relevant to almost any other article, but this one is somewhat of an exception. The Site (at the time of this tale) is a ramshackle observation facility in the middle of nowhere set up by a couple of Soviet scientists to monitor and study a poorly understood anomaly (not GRU Division "P"). Due to only functioning as observation of a static anomaly which presents no immediate danger to its surrounds (unless one enters it), there would most likely to no weapons stored on-Site (lack of funding/unnecessary)1. Dr Vasiliev himself mentions that they tried sending in soldiers with recording equipment, but they didn't return.
However, even if there were weapons on-Site (and the scientists had basic combat training), they would understand that firing bullets at something that doesn't exist has as much of an effect as sneezing on it, or asking it politely to leave.
There'd probably be security, sure, but it would be far outside the Site to (as I mentioned in my footnote) prevent people from intruding.
I think that's how things would work, correct me if I'm wrong.

Anyway, thanks for the recrit, hope this clarifies some things!

Footnotes
1. Maybe a couple to prevent people from intruding, but even then the weapon supply would be minimal.

item.title: Re: Hospital that heals you on its own.
item.content:encoded:
You have a lot of unique ideas. Even in the well explored field of medical SCPs you have something that I haven’t seen before. However it seems like you have too many ideas. Every line you’re introducing something new and it makes me wonder what this article would actually be about. I’d recommend revising it. I could see an entire article about “a hospital that tries to turn anything into a healthy human” at the same time I could see “a hospital that cures diseases with strange treatments”. It just feels like too much is happening at once in your current pitch with you talking about difficult containment procedures, cross-testing, and a researcher exploiting the SCP all at the same time. I think you should pick some. My recommendation is to focus on how it tries to transform things into people and throw in the containment difficulties. I’m a little biased because those are just my personal favorites but I also think they have the most potential.

item.title: Lock and ___
item.content:encoded:
I've posted this one before and intended to approach people directly for reviews, but I've been busy and it's been well over two weeks now since the last post so I thought I'd give the forum one last shot! I have made minor alterations due to the feedback I did receive last time (not from an official reviewer but helpful feedback nonetheless).

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Pretty standard SCP article layout, but I’m going to make use of drop-down “click to reveal” sections to help break down the length.

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a 1 m3 metal safe that cannot be opened or damaged by any apparent means. It causes auditory hallucinations in those who stand within 15 m of it for more than 3 hours (cumulative) that tempt them to try to open it. Effect is purely proximity-based – object safely observable from a distance. 3 – 72 hours after hallucinations begin, these victims convert into anomalous humanoids with an innate knowledge of SCP-XXXX’s location and resistance to anaesthetic and amnestics. Each of these beings will stick to 1 of 2 distinct behaviour patterns:

  • SCP-XXXX-1 – “Searchers”. Search obsessively for an alleged key to SCP-XXXX when able. Can become frustrated and violent at times. Lucid and capable of conversation, highly manipulative.
  • SCP-XXXX-2 – Animalistic. Repeatedly attempts to open SCP-XXXX by force, overriding any other behavioural drives. Incapable of conversation.
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: Features an extensive discovery report on the first emergence of the later-named SCP-XXXX-1, leading to discovery of XXXX and XXXX-2. Also features a report on a recurring incident with SCP-XXXX that the Foundation is still studying. References are made several times to a specific named researcher and her hypotheses/findings at several points to help give a connected narrative feel.
Tried to give the article a progressive narrative, in that SCP-XXXX seems relatively simple at first but every new thing we learn makes it seem more and more trouble.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: As previously mentioned, progressive nature of the article meant to gradually increase intrigue.

An incident report states that motion sensors within cell are often tripped and cameras deactivated, only for guards to find the cell completely undisturbed and equipment behaving normally again once they get there (incident does not repeat when SCP-XXXX is under constant guard), suggesting perhaps SCP-XXXX is starting to show awareness and more physically active behaviours, or possibly just messing with electrical equipment (still being studied at “time of report”).

Section at end reveals that an SCP-XXXX-1 instance claimed SCP-XXXX’s area of effect would begin expanding, causing the Foundation to regularly test its size, but SCP-XXXX-1 may have been lying and no changes have yet been detected.

Basically, I’m trying to give the sense with both of these parts that this SCP may or may not be a ticking time bomb of sorts.

Additional Notes: As this is my first SCP idea I’m sure it has plenty of issues all over, so please fire away!

item.title: ""Bureaucracy""
item.content:encoded:
This is one of the most incompetent portrayals of the Foundation I've ever seen. Receiving a series of direct emails about a Keter class anomaly that's kicking everyone's ass for months and months, and they can't even manage to acknowledge or send one reply; let alone think to resolve the issue. And it's explained away, not by depicting a small-scale Foundation without the available resources themselves; but by a Foundation apparently just too big and self-important to care.

The fines thing confuses me too. Is this something the Foundation has typically done before? How do they enforce payment of fines; do they have an appeals court for disputed infractions; is there any neutral arbitration? Or is this extortion bit meant to make the Foundation come off as cruel villains in this piece? Because if you're saying that the Foundation were deliberately ignoring the situation as it played out, then this potentially reads to me like some kind of convoluted caroonish scheme to get rid of Wilson's by driving them to bankruptcy. But I'm doubtful that was the intent.

(P.S.: -5° C is below freezing, even for salt water.)

item.title: Re: Abiogenesis (SCP)
item.content:encoded:
(Can’t give green lights)
Firstly, I really like the idea. I’m a big of fan of sci-fi plots like this one and think this has a lot of potential.

Secondly, I think the plot of an article like this would really benefit from a personal perspective. Some logs detailing the captain’s and the foundation’s reaction to learning about the origin of life being from humans and how their ideas about the universe change. Perhaps you have the captain or researcher be a religious man, despite working with anomalies everyday. A realization such as this would force them to challenge their beliefs and would add to the intrigue of the story.

Being careful not to make the plot too convoluted or confusing in a story like this is also important. Keeping things simple yet intriguing will provide food for thought and cut down on questions that ruin this kind of plot.

item.title: Re: Greenlight Request: A Second Reflection
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.

It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.

Once in containment, SCP-XXXX does not require any sort of furniture in its containment cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), only needing a cooling system to keep it from phasing out of the room. It does need to be fed, and its meals consist of wild animals and, if a test takes an unfortunate turn, an unlucky Class-D personnel.

It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell, and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment. This aggression is seemingly nullified while SCP-XXXX is in the presence of SCP-XXXX-B.

SCP-XXXX-B is the infant born from SCP-XXXX. It resembles a humanoid infant with lighter colored skin than its parent. It shares the same invisibility as its parent, but has not yet displayed any signs of aggression.

Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.

At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.

In the months following the containment of SCP-XXXX, it is discovered to have been pregnant, and it gives birth to SCP-XXXX-B while in containment. This, followed by repeated sightings of SCP-XXXX out in the wild despite it being in containment confirms that SCP-XXXX is not an isolated anomaly, but an entire species of creatures with the same abilities.

item.title: Hospital that heals you on its own.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A hospital, in a relatively populated area. Anyone who is sick, or injured, that walks in, will start to recover or heal, across the course of a few days to a few months, depending. Non-human life mutates, as if it's trying to become human, and ends up dead. Broken or damaged artificial objects 'heal' over with human biological components. 'Nurse' entities appear as body disposal, and to move immobile 'patients' to a bed. Where they come from is unknown, but they don't heal, they just don't die.

Central Narrative: On the worldbuilding side, this'll be in a relatively populated area, and may require not only fancy containment procedures, due to the hospital keeping itself looking in working order, and sending out "appointment" letters to the local area, somehow aware of illness or injury within a certain radius of it. Given its location, it may also require cooperation with a GoI, or local authorities, or some sort of group outside of the foundation. Perhaps it got discovered by two at a roughly similar time, or otherwise the foundation had it first, but then some other group (likely the GOC given they are, to my knowledge, the most able to show their faces in public, or the UIU if I put this in the states) turns up.

Experiment wise, it'll probably be a case of them trying to see how far it'll go, finding it can cure anomalous diseases (if the patient is still alive and human), and injuries, as well as things not thought fixable by modern medicine. Perhaps implication of some researcher using it for personal use, and getting into a lot of trouble for it, along with the expected D-Class abuse to see just what this thing can heal. Some stuff as well with the nurses, finding they're non-hostile, but trying to figure out where they come from, only to discover they're the patients that don't make it, put together into the nurses, and animated by unknown means.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I'd like to think the hospital itself is pretty unique, but I'd also use this as a sort of way of tying a few other SCPs together, those that are disease based, or cause funky injuries, and how the hospital tries to "fix" them. The slower time scale means that whilst telling why things are healing is impossible, observing what specifically is happening isn't. The nurses being non-hostile and non-belligerent also aids to this, since they can just put researchers in there with the D-Class to see what happens day by day.

Additional Notes: This is the first SCP I'll have ever tried to write. I've been reading for a good while, but my knowledge isn't encyclopaedic. Any ideas off of the vaguer points here would be greatly appreciated, and again I'm very sorry if this is too close to something that already exists.

item.title: Re: Deletions 70: If the fact will not fit the theory – let the theory go.
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5138 was found in a barn in 1979. A farmer looked melted and in 1 pen was SCP-5138. SCP-5138 appears to be a chicken and turkey combined that leaves behind radioactive waste that is similar to the acidity of hydrochloric acid. This radioactive waste is known as SCP-5138-2. SCP-5138-1 instances are eggs laid by SCP-5138. They will taste like anything the consumer is craving and then will fill the consumer with joy. 10 minutes after eating SCP-5138-1 will start to melt you from the inside out. Any living thing breathing SCP-5138-2 will go unconscious and when woken up will instantly go mad. Once 2 minutes pass, the victim will see hallucinations. After 10 minutes, the victim will start wandering around acting like different barn animals. Then finally after 12 minutes the victim will scream in pain then fall to the ground. SCP-5138-1 when hatched immediately grows and becomes an adult. Studies on how this happens are still going on.

Deleted at -20 and three votes.

SCP-5133 is a 1.6m tall bipedal insectoid entity, structured and patterned similarly to a female convergent lady beetle, (Hippodamia convergens) though it only has 4 limbs. Though wings are present in the subject, they are only vestigial.

Deleted at -12 and three votes.

Feedback Ported:

Quadraginta

+ show block
– hide block

It's a wish-fulfilling humanoid bug person. That in and of itself could have led to something interesting and meaningful if this concept went anywhere with it. Instead, we got an extremely short test log with the only personality being, 'I like to eat larva and I need good sleep.'

While reading this, I got the absolute barebones feeling this thing had the a childlike innocence, but it was so minimal, it didn't matter in the end.

Apologies if this is harsh. -1.

SCP-5232 is a six-sided silver dice of unknown origin (See addendum SCP-5232-1 for more details).SCP-5232 does not manifest any anomalous properties until an entity (humans, animals,or plants) comes within 3m2 of SCP-5232. If an entity comes within the aforementioned area, the dice will proceed to roll itself through unknown means, which tests have shown is completely randomized. (See SCP-5232 testing log for more details.)

Deleted at -12 and three votes. Rewrite by TheAnimateFry pending.

SCP-5667 is an autonomous, whole grain loaf of bread. Upon being damaged, SCP-5667 will regenerate damaged parts using contacting materials. When in contact with solid materials, a grey doughy substance will grow upon SCP-5667 filling and repairing any damaged areas of SCP-5667. This doughy substance will then harden and take on a more bread-like structure. Further analysis of the growth will reveal it to have the same chemical makeup as whatever material SCP-5667 was in physical contact with during the regeneration process. This process has been referred to as “the solid repairment effect” and can take from 30 minutes to 5 hours depending on the solidity of the materials used.

item.title: The Old Lady's House / Get Out, Intruder (open to critique and/or greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Fairly simple. The usual "number + class + SCP + description" block, followed by logs about the discovery of the item and research led on it.

[From here: 386 words]

Elevator Pitch: House is "haunted" after the passing of its previous inhabitant; TV screen in the kitchen warns anyone who stays too long in the kitchen, then the house proceeds to kill/absorb them if the warning is ignored.

Central Narrative: A grandma who used to live alone in her small, residential street house, passes away. Since then, the house considers any human (or any large enough animal – cats are an exception) as an intruder, and proceeds to warn them through a three-step vague set of warnings displayed on the kitchen's TV set. If the warnings are ignored, the "intruder" is then killed and absorbed by the house; their remains are found in a locker somewhere in the house (or perhaps in the garden?).

Possible ramifications:

+ show block
– hide block
  • If the TV is unplugged or turned off, warnings aren't displayed yet the house kills intruders anyway.
  • People exposed to the warnings, but who left the house after the 2nd warning (therefore ignoring the 1st one), might be similarly warned by the TV set of their own home, and therefore risk getting killed in the same fashion (the "effect" "follows" them)
  • One of the logs has a D-Class almost leaving the house in time, but they trip; most of their body is outside of the house when the absorption event begins, but the house absorbs their toes, which stayed inside when the event occured
  • Cats are unaffected because the old lady gave them shelter in the house (relevance?)
  • Bringing the old lady's corpse back to the house stops the effect (would it strip away any interest from the SCP article, or (oppositely) be considered as an appropriate form of containment?)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I have absolutely no idea about what would make this idea special. I'm not very ambitious.

Additional Notes: This is an idea which appeared to me after binge-reading some entries on this website. I think I can pull off the "number + class + SCP + description" block, but I am worried about how I could build a backstory behind it. I figure the old lady could be a start, but I think I'm a bit "weak" in that area (I want it to be a bit more than just a house which kills people: why does it consider other people as "intruders"? does the old lady have a story? etc)

Thank you for your attention and thanks in advance for any input!

item.title: Re: The Bartender
item.content:encoded:
I am not qualified to give greenlights yet. However, I think this is a decent concept. Here's my (albeit rudimentary) critique:

This contradicts itself. Saying 'targets' implies that your SCP is a predator that hunts down its prey using its anomalous sensing properties, yet then you say it's not hostile. Perhaps you might want to word that differently.

Next, how does it find its targets? Echolocation? Heat sensing? Anomalous means? You might want to specify that and how the Foundation found that out.

What kind of disturbances in reality? I'm confused… you just listed what emotions it felt. Or maybe that was supposed to be symptoms of being around it. That would be a cognitohazard or maybe memetic hazard. Even so, if the footnote was supposed to be its behaviour, that again contradicts the earlier statement about it being non-hostile.

Have a nice day!

First of all, thanks for replying my comment. And by no means I think my ramblings have to be the final say on anything.

I just reread the article, paid attention, and keep my opinions:

1- Show, don't tell. The article doesn't show any reason to think the current state won't change. If the last shut down included some hardware destruction and was followed by examination, maybe. But simply shutting down isn't a guarantee that an anomalous computer is out for good;

2- Indeed, but see above. Standard containment is enough only after the end of the anomalous properties is beyond doubt, given the risk of an anomalous reactivation causing a breach;

3- Yes, and yet it doesn't change that it sounds like a Task Force report to me and would be better put as such or be removed;

4- It is not only two details, it is the entirety of the second paragraph in the description and the way the first paragraph starts. The first paragraph makes it seems like being from AR is of more relevance than it being anomalous. This is an important info for the investigation, but this is not an investigation report. The second paragraph gives a lot of context and detail, to the extend of even revealing its initial auction price;

5- Missed this, sorry.

My problem with all the context given is that it takes a lot of space, but have no bearing on the core of the article. And no, even it being from AR isn't important, it is *interesting*, but not important.

From an In-Character perspective an SCP article is mainly about the object being studied, so the focus of the text matters. From an OoC perspective it sounds like those details will have some relevance when they won't, at the same time that a proper description of effects and tests is lacking. It is a bad frame for the core concept.

But again, this is my impression and criticism. You only have to take from it what makes sense for you. You can argue otherwise, I'm just saying up front that I write a lot and that can seem to be contentious, it seems. And I do over-explain.

That's your choice entirely. You know what? I say we could sit around here for ages talking about what could work and what couldn't. If there's one thing I've learned from learning how to draw, it's that things never end up on paper like you imagine them. So, write up a draft in the sandbox. Just establish the main story points and try to connect them up. That way you'll know for certain. Trust me, I understand this dillema.

And hey, it's a win-win scenario either way: If your draft is good, then you won't have thrown a great idea away. If it's shit, you'll know for a fact and you'll learn from your mistake. And on top of that, you'll get actual writing experience. I'll even crit it if you want.

No-vote. The UIU storyline is interesting enough, but the testing logs are basically unrelated to the arc. It also would have been cooler to see more interaction about the funding issue of the UIU. Anyway, A few nitpicks,

+ Nitpicks
- Close

WARNING: Access to this section of this document is restricted to O5 Councilmembers and the Site Directors of Site-64. If you hold sufficient clearance, proceed below

A Space is needed here.

Despite its tightly packed molecular structure, SCP-5290 is transparent and features no coloring.

This sentence contains a redundancy. If something is transparent it features no colour by definition.

Upon losing contact with the object or losing consciousness, a version will disconnect from the group consciousness.

The clinical tone is off here. Maybe say "Upon losing contact with the object or losing consciousness, contact with a separate version will be lost." This would probably make more sense if the person was designated as a SCP-5290-1 instance.

[DATA EXPUNGED] USD

Why is this expunged? It doesn't seem that any damage would be caused by knowing how much money someone had.

(Note, Agent Nord may have stolen other anomalous objects and sold them to other parties before being apprehended)

This should probably be in a footnote.

I think all of the writing is fine otherwise.
